vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Lagrangian & Hamiltonian Mechanics
vertices.description: The variational principle, Euler-Lagrange equations, Hamiltonians, phase space, and Noether's theorem linking symmetries to conservation laws.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Self-reported beginner level. Knows concepts (Lagrangians, Hamiltonians, variational principles, Noether's theorem) through project context but cannot do the math independently. Uses Lagrangians throughout the project (Son's L=P(X)) without deep variational intuition.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Quantum Mechanics Foundations
vertices.description: Wave-particle duality, Hilbert spaces, operators, the Schrödinger equation, path integrals, and the measurement problem.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Intermediate QFT/EFT experience implies working knowledge of QM foundations. Understands path integrals conceptually through the EFT context. Knows the Madelung transform connection. Gap is in computational fluency and deep intuition for why quantum mechanics works the way it does.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Statistical Mechanics & Thermal Physics
vertices.description: Partition functions, ensembles, the Boltzmann distribution, free energy, entropy, phase transitions, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Self-reported beginner. Familiar with key concepts (partition functions, thermal equilibrium, FDR) through the SK-EFT context but hasn't built deep foundations independently. This is a critical gap — the KMS condition and FDR are central to the program and require solid stat mech intuition.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Fluid Dynamics Fundamentals
vertices.description: Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, compressible vs incompressible flow, sound waves, viscosity, and transport coefficients.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Wrote transonic_background.py, works extensively with BEC flow profiles, understands transonic backgrounds and sonic horizons through the project. Intermediate BEC/condensed matter experience. The physical substrate is familiar but the formal fluid dynamics (Navier-Stokes derivation, Reynolds number, etc.) may be less developed.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: EFT Philosophy & Derivative Expansion
vertices.description: The Wilsonian paradigm: physics at different scales decouples; low-energy physics is described by the most general action compatible with symmetries, organized by a derivative expansion.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Intermediate QFT/EFT — understands Wilsonian approach, derivative expansion, power counting through the project. The entire research program is built on EFT thinking. Transfer pathway (0.75 similarity) from QFT background. Gap is visceral feel for why higher-order terms are literally 'smaller physics' — needs to move from knowing the rules to feeling the logic.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Son's Superfluid EFT: L = P(X)
vertices.description: The leading-order effective field theory for a superfluid: a single Goldstone boson ψ with Lagrangian L = P(X), X = (∂ψ)².

learner_state.evidence_summary: Knows Son's EFT from the project — central to Phase 1. Understands it's a Goldstone boson for broken U(1). Transfer 0.7 (far) from QFT background. Gap: building intuition for WHY L=P(X) is the unique answer requires deeper comfort with symmetry arguments and SSB.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking & Goldstone Modes
vertices.description: When the ground state has less symmetry than the Lagrangian, massless Goldstone bosons appear. The phonon is the Goldstone of broken U(1) in a superfluid.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Knows SSB conceptually — Mexican hat potential, Goldstone theorem, phonon as Goldstone boson. Uses SSB in both the superfluid EFT (U(1) breaking) and ADW mechanism (GL(4,R) → SO(3,1)). Gap is deep intuition for the mechanism and its inevitability.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: BEC Physics & Bogoliubov Theory
vertices.description: Bose-Einstein condensation, the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, Bogoliubov transformation, healing length ξ, and the dispersion relation.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Intermediate BEC/condensed matter experience. Engaged deeply with BEC physics through the project — knows experimental parameters for all three platforms (Steinhauer, Heidelberg, Trento), Bogoliubov theory, transonic flows, superfluid order parameters. Transfer 0.75. Gap is microscopic physical intuition — why atoms condense, what healing length physically represents.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: The Acoustic Metric & Analog Gravity
vertices.description: Sound waves in a moving fluid propagate on an effective curved spacetime. Sonic horizons form where v = c_s.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Gateway node. Knows the acoustic metric formula, understands Unruh-Visser derivation structurally. AcousticMetric.lean proves 4 key theorems they designed. Transfer 0.75 from GR background. Gap: feeling how the metric emerges inevitably from linearized fluid equations — the geometric perspective, not just the formula.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Hawking Radiation & the Trans-Planckian Problem
vertices.description: A sonic horizon emits thermal phonons at T_H = ℏκ/2πk_B. The trans-Planckian problem: do UV physics matter?

learner_state.evidence_summary: Gateway node. Knows the formula, understands the trans-Planckian problem, knows why BEC experiments are the testing ground. The entire program is about Hawking radiation corrections. Transfer 0.7 from GR. Gap: deep intuition for WHY horizons radiate — the mode-mixing picture, not just the formula.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Transonic Flow & Sonic Horizons in BEC
vertices.description: Setting up 1D transonic backgrounds with v(x_H) = c_s(x_H) at the horizon. Surface gravity κ and experimental parameters.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Wrote transonic_background.py. Knows the physical setup, the three experimental platforms, the adiabaticity parameter D = κξ/c_s. Solid working knowledge from code development. Gap: deeper physical feel for the flow topology.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: The Schwinger-Keldysh Contour
vertices.description: The SK contour doubles DOF to compute real-time correlators in thermal/mixed states. Physical fields ψ_r and noise fields ψ_a.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Gateway node. Central to the entire project — SKDoubling.lean has 9 theorems they designed. Knows the forward/backward branch structure, r/a field decomposition. Gap: physical intuition for WHY we need to double — the deep connection between real-time physics and the contour structure.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: KMS Symmetry & Fluctuation-Dissipation Relations
vertices.description: The KMS condition encodes thermal equilibrium: ψ_a → ψ_a + iβ∂_t ψ_r. Generates FDR automatically.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Knows the KMS condition from the project. Discovered the Aristotle counterexample that broke the original KMSSymmetry. CGLTransform.lean derives FDR. Gap: physical intuition for what KMS means beyond the formula — why dissipation and noise must be linked by temperature.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: SK Axioms: Normalization, Positivity, KMS
vertices.description: Three axioms constraining the SK action: normalization, positivity (unitarity), KMS (thermal equilibrium). Together they determine the action up to transport coefficients.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Designed the Lean proofs (SKDoubling.lean) that verify these axioms constrain 9 terms → 2 free parameters. Knows the result and the proof structure. Gap: physical feel for each axiom — why positivity means probability conservation, what normalization physically requires.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: First-Order Dissipative Hawking Correction
vertices.description: T_eff = T_H(1 + δ_disp + δ_diss + δ_cross), where δ_diss = Γ_H/κ is the new dissipative correction.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Central node. Transfer 0.85 (near) — designed the entire Phase 1 calculation, wrote Paper 1, designed the Lean proofs. Knows the result, the derivation structure, and the experimental numbers. Gap is the critical one identified in the dossier: knowing WHAT vs feeling WHY — physical intuition for why each step is inevitable.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Transport Coefficient Counting & Higher Orders
vertices.description: count(N) = ⌊(N+1)/2⌋ + 1. Parity alternation theorem: odd orders parity-preserving, even orders require parity breaking.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Knows the counting formula and parity alternation theorem from the project. enumeration.py validates the counting; SecondOrderSK.lean and ThirdOrderSK.lean prove the results. Gap: intuition for WHY parity matters and how it connects to the background flow breaking spatial symmetry.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Frequency-Dependent Spectral Distortion
vertices.description: Second-order correction δ^(2)(ω) ∝ ω³ — spectrum deviates from Planckian. On-shell vanishing via positivity constraint.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Knows from the project that on-shell vanishing was discovered during Aristotle Round 4. Understands the result structurally. Gap: physical intuition for why frequency-dependent corrections are qualitatively different from temperature shifts, and what on-shell vanishing means physically.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: CGL Dynamical KMS Derivation
vertices.description: The Crossley-Glorioso-Liu master formula pairing noise with odd-in-ω dissipative terms.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Recently completed Phase 2D work — CGL derivation, 7 Lean theorems. Knows the chain: CGL FDR → T-reversal → model identification → FirstOrderKMS. Gap: physical content of the CGL formula — why noise comes from the antisymmetric part.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: WKB Connection Formula & Complex Turning Points
vertices.description: Exact WKB for the dissipative mode equation. Complex turning point shift, Stokes geometry, modified Bogoliubov coefficients, three non-perturbative effects.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Designed Paper 4 with 17 Lean theorems. Knows the results: modified unitarity, FDR noise floor, spectral floor. Gap: physical intuition for complex turning points, what modified unitarity means for information loss, and the Stokes geometry picture.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Bogoliubov Coefficients & Particle Creation
vertices.description: Mode mixing at a horizon: |β_k|² gives particle spectrum. Standard Hawking: n_k = Planck distribution.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Knows Bogoliubov coefficients from the project — bogoliubov.py computes modified coefficients. Understands that |β_k|² gives particle number. Gap: physical intuition for how mode mixing creates particles — the conceptual leap from classical waves to quantum particle creation.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Higher-Form Symmetries & Gauge Structure
vertices.description: Generalized symmetries where conserved charge lives on p-dimensional submanifolds. Key: higher-form symmetries must be Abelian.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Knows the concept from the gauge erasure work — understands that 1-form symmetries act on Wilson loops and must be Abelian. Gap: deep intuition for WHY higher-form symmetries must be Abelian (operators on codimension >1 submanifolds commute) and the physical picture of the photon as a Goldstone.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Non-Abelian Gauge Erasure Theorem
vertices.description: Non-Abelian gauge DOF universally erased by hydrodynamization. U(1) survives (photonization). The most important negative result.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Wrote Paper 3 and GaugeErasure.lean (11 theorems + 1 axiom). Knows the argument chain, the N=4 SYM case, the SM analysis. Gap: feeling the inevitability of the result — why non-Abelian gauge info MUST be lost in the fluid limit, not just that it IS.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: ADW Mechanism: Emergent Tetrad Gravity
vertices.description: Multi-fermion interaction produces tetrad condensate via SSB: GL(4,R) → SO(3,1). 2 massless spin-2 gravitons emerge as Goldstone bosons.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Wrote Paper 5 with 21 Lean theorems. Knows the breaking pattern, mode counting, Coleman-Weinberg mechanism, 4 structural obstacles. Gap: the conceptual leap that spacetime geometry emerges from fermion condensation — this requires genuine rethinking of what geometry IS.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Vestigial Gravity (Level 1)
vertices.description: Composite metric g_μν without coherent tetrad VEV. Three-phase structure: pre-geometric → vestigial → full tetrad. EP violation predicted.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Wrote Paper 6 with Monte Carlo simulation. Knows the three-phase structure, EP violation prediction, lattice model. Gap: physical intuition for what a composite order parameter means and why it can have different symmetry from the elementary field.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Coleman-Weinberg Effective Potential
vertices.description: One-loop quantum corrections trigger SSB: fermion determinant gives V_eff. Critical coupling G_c.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Knows from Paper 5 context — gap_equation.py computes V_eff, hubbard_stratonovich.py sets up the decomposition. Understands structurally. Gap: physical intuition for what 'integrating out fermions' means and how radiative corrections trigger symmetry breaking.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Fracton Hydrodynamics & Information Retention
vertices.description: Fractons with restricted mobility. Conserving charge + dipole + higher multipoles retains exponentially more UV info than Navier-Stokes.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Wrote Phase 4 fracton code (sk_eft.py, information_retention.py, FractonHydro.lean). Knows restricted mobility concept, conservation laws, information retention comparison. Gap: physical intuition for fractons — why restricted mobility changes everything about hydrodynamics.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: String-Net Condensation & Topological Order

learner_state.evidence_summary: Conceptual exposure through the Critical Review and hybrid architecture design. Knows string-nets are Layer 1 providing gauge structure. Gap: significant — topological order and string-net condensation are conceptually rich and require dedicated learning. Currently at the vocabulary level.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Transfer 0.9 (near). Wrote the Critical Review v3 articulating all three walls. Knows the assessment, the status of each wall, what would change the picture. Gap: moving from documented assessment to felt understanding of the obstruction mechanisms — understanding at the physics level, not just the narrative level.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: BEC Experimental Landscape
vertices.description: Steinhauer, Heidelberg, Trento, Paris polariton. Platform-specific predictions from the SK-EFT.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Wrote predictions.py and prediction_tables.tex. Knows the experimental groups, platform parameters, what each offers uniquely. Gap: deeper physical understanding of the experimental challenges and what distinguishes good from great Hawking measurements.

gap_analysis.effective_scope_estimate: You already cover ~47% of the impact-weighted graph at the 'familiar' level — you know the vocabulary, the results, and the narrative for almost everything. The curriculum doesn't need to teach you what these concepts ARE; it needs to build physical intuition for WHY they work. This dramatically compresses the curriculum: instead of a 12-month ground-up physics education, you need a ~6-8 month intuition-building program. The two genuine foundation gaps (statistical mechanics and Lagrangian mechanics) need ~4-6 weeks of dedicated early work; after that, your project familiarity accelerates every subsequent topic. Estimated total: 120-160 sessions at 45 min/day, 5 days/week.
